title: AI: Learning Styles
welcome_lead: How machines learn from data — three big paradigms.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning.
final_note: Match the learning style to the data you have.

concepts.def: Learning from labelled examples to predict outputs.
Finding structure in unlabelled data, e.g. clusters.
Learning by reward signals from interaction with an environment.
Data used to fit a model's parameters.
Held-out data used to estimate model performance.
The correct answer attached to a training example.

walkthroughs.body_html: Supervised models learn a function from inputs to labels — classification (cat vs dog) or regression (price). Common methods include decision trees, linear regression and neural networks.
Unsupervised models find structure without labels — k-means clustering groups similar points; PCA reduces dimensions. Useful for exploration and segmentation.
Reinforcement learning trains an agent that takes actions and receives rewards. AlphaGo and self-driving controllers use it. The agent learns a policy that maximises long-term reward.
